vpn: Increase charon RLIMIT_AS to 750MB Prior to this change, charon was being started by vpn-manager without explicitly changing the RLIMIT_AS. In this case, it was inheriting the limits of its parent(s), going back to shill's soft limit of 200MB. As charon tends to have a somewhat large VmSize, we want RLIMIT_AS to be greater than shill's. Manual tests have shown VmPeak hovering around ~360MB given some L2TP configurations. Setting the limit to 750MB for some breathing room, as Charon's VmPeak has been seen to be quite large given certain configurations. BUG=chromium:961519 TEST=-All unit tests are passing. -Consistently connecting to an L2TP configuration that was previously failing on my Nautilus, with both strongswan 5.5.3 and 5.7.2. -Changing the limit to 100MB causes the connection to fail every time. Change-Id: Icea0488eb64cdc786357592ebca282928515ffdf Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1757203 Tested-by: Alex Khouderchah <akhouderchah@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: Alex Khouderchah <akhouderchah@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org>

faft: Initialize the FirmwareUpdater lazily. Instead of extracting the shellball right at start, which takes time and can raise errors, now the rpc call handler won't initialize the FirmwareUpdater until a test actually goes to use one of its methods. This should help with debugging the disappearance of the manifest file, and prevent it from blocking tests that don't use the updater. etphidiap: Upgrade from etphidiap-1.1 to etphidiap-1.3 BUG=b:133112560 TEST=Built OS image, installed it on 4 DUTs covering: 4 build phases 3 touchpad hardware revision identifiers 2 actual touchpad hardware revisions Then on all DUTs: Confirmed etphid_updater still present. Tested -b (reflashing) in both hidraw and i2c modes. Tested -g, -m, -w options with 9 touchpad firmware versions: 0x09 0x0B 0x0C 0x0D 0x0E 0x0F 0x10 0x11 0x13 (debug build) Tested -b, -g, -m, -w options in i2c mode with corrupted firmware. Confirmed touch updater wrappers still invoked and succeeded on boot when no update expected (no update was applied). Confirmed touch updater wrappers still invoked and succeeded on boot when update was expected (update was correctly applied). The -g output (firmware version) continued to work as before. The -m output was consistent in all situations, as expected. The -w output was unexpectedly inconsistent depending on the current firmware version. See the bug for details. However since that option is not used by the updater wrapper yet, its behavior is currently immaterial, this uprev need not be blocked on understanding the inconsistencies. Change-Id: I0502dacb58b548fd956e91658c1c6ed5fd1a3652 Signed-off-by: Matthew Blecker <matthewb@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1758205 Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Bob Moragues <moragues@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: YH Lin <yueherngl@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Harry Cutts <hcutts@chromium.org>
